# MCPJam API

> Programmatic acces
s to the MCP servers in your MCPJam projects: diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.\n\n> [!WARNIN

G]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but
> it has not been generally announced and
the surface may change, including in\n> breaking ways, while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors docume
nted on this page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on

[Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or
> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API ke

y](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'l
l be asked to sign in and then land right back on the API keys page.\n\nThe MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in y
our\n[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects (from CI, scripts, or your own agents)\nwithout opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resources**: list your projects, their servers, eval
 suites, and chat s
essions, so every ID the other routes need is\n self-serve\n* **Validate a server**: connect, initialize, and capture a capabilit
y snapshot\n* **Run the doctor**: the probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements**: does t
his server need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and resources**: the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a
prompt**: execute primitives and get the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot**: to
ols, resources, and prompts as one JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients**: list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n tem
plate like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations
that define how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its
`configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n config change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename (a rename\n does
not rotate the config, so the config token cannot detect a concurrent\n one), and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silen
tly reverted\n* **Manage a project's environments**: list, read, and archive the named\n execution bundles (host + optional serve

r group) that eval
 suites and goals run against,
 and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it
* **List a projec
t's studies**: name, access mode, attached servers, and\n share link, and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,\n
tool-approval policy, and resolved servers\n* **Author eval suites**: create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test
cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously**:
create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\
n usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,\n tagged `source: \"api\"`\n* **Manage a server's account
s**: complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n acco
unt; list, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\n write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless age
nt turn**: send a message history, get back the\n assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resou
rces it created (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned\n server-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedback**:
report a bug, a missing capability, or something\n confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the\

n `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted inspector

. Managing API keys remains UI-only; see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"

css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the bas

e
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"the
me\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n

-H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key\
n\n1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)\n in the hosted app (the card at the top of this

page takes you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.
3. Copy

the key (`sk_…`) immediately; **it is shown exactly once** and never
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revo

ked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organizatio
n at creation and acts **as you,\ninside that organization**. Per-request authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if th

e key's owner can access that project and server. A key
can never reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two

deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface
>
with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> the UI.\n> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API

.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable
or secret manager; never commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integ
ration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n

* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in
 [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `
401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used; crea

te a new key
from [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers
are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads**, the catalog listings and eval-run polling, are\n`GET` and tak

e their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource object directly |
| Collection | `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor\
": \"...\" }`; `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }

` with a matching HTTP status |

**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `cu
